(4)  If a secured party has an interest in an accession that
has priority over the claim of any  person having an interest
in the whole, the secured party may, on default and subject
to the provisions of this Act relating to default, remove the
accession from the whole, if, unless otherwise agreed, the
secured party reimburses any person having an encumbrance
or the owner of the whole of the goods who is not the debtor,
for  the  cost  of  repairing  any  physical  injury,  excluding
diminution in value of the whole caused by the absence of
the accession or by the necessity of replacement.
(5)    A  person  entitled  to  any  reimbursement  under
subsection  (4)  may  refuse  permission  to  remove  the
accession, until the secured party has given adequate security
for the reimbursement.
